audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers agreed with each other but disagreed with the packet chart and the mirror: Level 6 was given to Ryze and 2+ items to Akali, while the page's own whys[4] describes Akali executing a poked Ryze and whys[6] describes Ryze reclaiming the fight at two items.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Ryze/Skill/Akali/Akali/Akali/Akali/Ryze, and the already-audited mirror (akali__ryze) flipped Level 6 to Akali and 2+ items to Ryze. Perfect Execution at 6 is a kill button on a poked Ryze; a completed Seraph's Ryze cannot be one-shot.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side and win[4] to Akali, phases[6].side and win[6] to Ryze, proposed as matched pairs, with ratings inverted from the mirror (Level 6 3/10, 2+ items 6/10) and the two templated whys rewritten so the prose no longer argues the opposite side.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls Twilight Shroud a "fifteen-second" cooldown; phases[5].why claimed Ryze's first item flips the lane while the same row is scored for Akali.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20/19/18/17/16 — twenty seconds at rank 1, never fifteen. The first-item row belongs to Akali because Rocketbelt lands before Seraph's does.
audit.corrected: Shroud window stated as 20 seconds at rank 1; the first-item row's why now describes her spike instead of Ryze's.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0], spikes[0].text and the early block all state Ryze "must walk to melee range" to use Q. dontsFull[0].d is placeholder filler and never states the burst tell.
audit.why: Overload (Q) is a 1000-range line projectile on a flat 5s cooldown; Five Point Strike is 550. Ryze out-ranges her by nearly double at level 1 — the advice inverted the one thing that makes level 1 his. Separately, Assassin's Mark rings a champion Akali has damaged with a spell and empowers her next attack when she leaves the ring, so the reset wind-up, not the ability cast, is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Q's 1000 range stated against her 550, and the Assassin's Mark ring/exit reset given as the burst tell in Critical Don'ts.

edits.before: Realm Warp opens flanks and escapes, and your EQ DPS now duels most tops on their cooldown gaps.
edits.after: Perfect Execution's two-part dash executes a poked Ryze — Realm Warp is an escape here, not a duel button.

edits.before: Rod of Ages ends the HP problem — your short trades become favourable on raw math.
edits.after: Rocketbelt closes your 615 root gap before Seraph's lands — her burst beats your HP curve.

edits.before: Ryze controls melee range with Q only but Akali's Five Point Strike is equally short-range — trade lands near even; use Q to deny her Passive mark stacking on the wave.
edits.after: Overload (Q) reaches 1000 units against her 550-range Five Point Strike, so the poke trade is yours on cooldown — use it to deny Assassin's Mark stacking on the wave.

edits.before: Ryze controls melee range with his Q threat — Akali's Five Point Strike poke is short, so respect the range but do not let her stack Passive marks for free.
edits.after: Overload (Q) outranges Five Point Strike 1000 to 550 — poke her off last hits from range and refuse to let Assassin's Mark stack on you for free.

edits.before: At level 1 you only have Q and must walk to melee range to trade — Akali's Five Point Strike poke is short-range too, so neither of you can bully the other cleanly, but she wins any exchange you let go long because her Passive mark stacks mean free poke. Shove the first wave quickly so Akali cannot freely walk up and stack marks; use Q at max range to harass her on last-hit attempts without committing to melee range. At level 2 your W root gives you the first real threat: if she steps up aggressively, W-root into empowered Q lands real damage and backs her off. Level 3 is where she tilts the math — E dash plus Twilight Shroud means she can start a trade, vanish mid-combo to dodge your W root, and finish with a full burst rotation. Do not walk into the shroud; if she activates W, disengage with Phase Rush and wait for the shroud to expire before re-engaging on your terms.
edits.after: At level 1 Overload (Q) throws 1000 units against her 550-range Five Point Strike, so you win the poke exchange outright as long as you never let it go long — Assassin's Mark rings you the moment she lands a spell, and walking out of that ring hands her a free empowered auto. Shove the first wave so she cannot stroll up and mark you, and harass her on last-hit attempts from the end of Q's range. At level 2 your W root gives you the first real threat: if she steps up, W-root into empowered Q lands real damage and backs her off. Level 3 tilts the math — E dash plus Twilight Shroud means she can open a trade, vanish mid-combo to break your W target, and finish the burst. Never walk into the shroud; if she drops W, leave on Phase Rush and wait the 20 seconds out before re-engaging on your terms.

edits.before: Akali burns Twilight Shroud on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Akali burns Twilight Shroud on nothing — take the 20-second rank-1 invitation.

edits.before: That’s Akali’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Her Assassin's Mark reset is the tell — leave the ring before that auto lands.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are false positives — Perfect Execution is Akali's real R name in both snippets. Ratings were inverted from the mirror's stated values (mirror gave Akali 7/10 at Level 6 and 4/10 at 2+ items). The full layer here is heavily templated and still refers to Akali as 'he'/'his' in breakdown.wave, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d and report[4]/report[9]; those are inherited boilerplate shared across the champion's matchups, not matchup facts, so they are left for a champion-level pass rather than rewritten one path at a time here.
